tasks.short: Measure customers and record their actual measurements

steps.what: Locate and verify the customer's measurement record for the garment order
inputs: customer-confirmed identity and garment order reference
existing customer measurement record if present

steps.what: Measure the customer using tape measures, checking posture, measurement points and uncertain readings
inputs: actual customer and tape measure
verified customer measurement form
outputs: actual tape measurements with identified measurement points and units

steps.what: Record actual measurements, units, date and fit observations for the customer
inputs: actual tape measurements with identified measurement points and units
verified customer measurement form

steps.what: Check the final recorded measurements against actual readings and approve the record version
inputs: complete actual customer measurement record
actual tape measurements with identified measurement points and units

steps.what: Save the approved measurements in the same customer measurement record
inputs: approved customer measurement record v1

tasks.design: Configure a garment-specific measurement form in the {OPS_SYSTEM} with fixed units and named measurement points. The tailor still takes tape measurements and enters every actual value; the form reuses the verified customer reference and reduces field navigation, followed by review and a separate save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right record and navigating a general-purpose measurement form can interrupt physical measuring.
tasks.enabler_now: Native form layouts can preselect relevant measurement fields and show units without inferring body dimensions.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate tape placement and interpretation of posture or fit remain hands-on work.
tasks.human_edge: Notice an implausible measurement and repeat it with the customer's comfort in mind.

ambition.what: No new fitting service or authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 for measurement-record access and permitted personal-data fields

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: configurable records forms can show fixed measurement labels and units and reuse verified customer references.

assumptions: Boundary includes taking and recording actual measurements. No scanner, smart tape, free transcript or automatic body measurement is assumed.

The customer supplies identity and order reference; the tailor checks them in s1 and produces actual point-labelled values in s2. s3 retains twenty hours for manual value capture, corrections and observations; no structured readings appear without that work.

Native form configuration first. This scenario assumes an existing order system with a general measurement form, not a historical paper or rekey baseline. If the form already matches the garment, the change yields no gain.
Shares and reductions are provisional design scenarios, not measurements. Same-system save is approximately zero effort today and remains fully retained at one-point granularity.
unknowns: Actual form layout and lookup effort
Existing measurement field and unit conventions
research_questions: Does a garment-specific layout reduce navigation without reducing value checks?
Can each recorded value be tied to the actual measurement point and unit?

already_counted.description: Enter and check actual measurements and observations

approvals.approved_version: approved customer measurement record v1; edits require s4 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 7 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 6.5. High allows 2.5 additional hours for unusual measurement fields; low applies when the current form already fits the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Estimate garment-making cost from actual time and material assumptions

steps.what: Retrieve the garment design, requested finish and relevant order specifications for the cost estimate
inputs: customer-order design and finish specifications with revision
existing garment pattern reference if available

steps.what: Estimate the garment's making time and material requirements, including difficult construction and waste allowances
inputs: checked garment estimation specification
tailor's actual inspection and construction knowledge
outputs: tailor-entered operation hours, material quantities, waste allowances and units

steps.what: Check the applicable material unit costs and authorised labour costing rate
inputs: tailor-entered operation hours, material quantities, waste allowances and units
finance-maintained dated material costs and authorised labour costing rates
outputs: checked unit costs and rate basis

steps.what: Calculate how much the garment will cost to make from the explicit time, materials and checked rates
inputs: tailor-entered operation hours, material quantities, waste allowances and units
checked unit costs and rate basis
outputs: complete calculated garment cost estimate with assumptions

steps.what: Assess estimate plausibility and finish the cost estimate with uncertainty and exclusions explicit
inputs: complete calculated garment cost estimate with assumptions
checked garment estimation specification

steps.what: Approve the final internal garment cost estimate version
inputs: complete reviewed garment cost estimate

steps.what: Save the approved cost estimate in the same garment order record
inputs: approved garment cost estimate v1

tasks.design: Configure the {OPS_SYSTEM} costing worksheet to reuse checked order specifications and authorised rates from the {ERP}. The tailor enters garment-specific time and material requirements, checks the deterministic calculation and approves the finished internal cost estimate before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated rate lookup and arithmetic can consume effort even when the difficult quantity estimates remain human.
tasks.enabler_now: Native costing formulas can multiply explicit hours and quantities by checked rates and preserve assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual fabrics, finishing work and uncertain construction time can dominate estimate accuracy.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which apparently simple garment details add substantial skilled work.

ambition.what: Compare the cost effect of an alternative fabric or finish before committing to a construction approach.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 for order and authorised cost access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: garment cost worksheets can calculate material and labour costs from explicit quantities, hours and unit rates.

assumptions: Boundary is estimating making cost and recording the estimate, not setting a selling price or issuing a customer quote. No external send is proposed or counted.

The order owner supplies design revision and finish requirements; finance supplies rate id, effective date, unit and amount. s2 explicitly counts human estimation and entry of hours, quantities and waste before any calculation.

Native costing configuration first. The scenario assumes repeated rate navigation and manual calculation inside an existing order record, not paper or second-system rekeying. If formulas already do this, the saving is zero.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Existing system runtime earns no labour saving; s4 remaining time checks units, totals and missing inputs. Same-system save stays fully retained.
unknowns: Existing native costing support and rates access
Actual effort in rate lookup and arithmetic
research_questions: Can an actual estimate be reproduced with explicit units and rate dates?
Do quantity uncertainties dominate the benefit of faster arithmetic?

already_counted.description: Check formulas, units and cost totals

incremental.description: Maintain rate mappings and costing formulas

approvals.approved_version: approved garment cost estimate v1; edits require s6 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 30 minus 1 upkeep gives 29. High allows six additional hours resolving missing costs and unit exceptions; low covers already configured formulas and rate views.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with customers about materials and garment styles

steps.what: Find the customer's current garment order and relevant style and material references
inputs: customer-confirmed order reference
existing material and style catalogue maintained by the workshop

steps.what: Confer with customers to determine the types of material and garment styles desired, using actual preferences and samples
inputs: checked order and discussion references
actual customer preferences and physical samples
outputs: actual discussed material and garment-style choices with open questions

steps.what: Record the customer's actual material and style choices and unresolved questions in the garment order
inputs: actual discussed material and garment-style choices with open questions
checked order and discussion references

steps.what: Check the final choice record for faithful meaning and approve its internal record version
inputs: complete draft customer choice record
actual discussed material and garment-style choices with open questions

steps.what: Save the approved customer choices in the same garment order record
inputs: approved customer choice record v1
outputs: stored customer material and style choices

tasks.design: Configure linked style and material references in the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}, and reuse the verified order and catalogue identifiers in the choice form. The tailor holds the actual conversation, captures the customer's meaning and approves the finished internal record before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference navigation and repeated order or sample identifiers can interrupt recording around a customer discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked records can reuse known identifiers while leaving actual preference capture to the tailor.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may express a desired feel or appearance without knowing which materials achieve it.
tasks.human_edge: Use samples, questions and fitting experience to translate a preference without imposing a style.

ambition.what: No additional service or decision right is assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked order forms can reuse catalogue identifiers while the person records customer choices and exceptions.

assumptions: Boundary includes reference lookup, discussion and the existing written garment-order choices. No customer time is counted in the focal denominator and no recording or transcript is assumed.

Workshop catalogue owners supply sample/style id and current description; the customer supplies the order reference. s1 checks these and s3 counts actual choice and uncertainty capture; known identifiers alone can be prefilled.

Native configuration first. s3 retains twelve hours for substantive recording and correction. If choices are not normally recorded, remove that component and remeasure rather than invent paperwork savings.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system saving is approximately zero effort and stays fully retained. There is no automatic customer confirmation send or production release.
research_questions: Does linking samples reduce navigation while preserving the customer's exact choice and unresolved questions?
Are native fields already configured this way?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual choices and unresolved questions

incremental.description: Maintain style/material links and choice form fields

approvals.approved_version: approved customer choice record v1; edits require s4 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 6 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 5.5. High allows 2.5 additional hours checking unusual sample references; low applies when existing linked forms already remove that effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read garment tags and determine required alterations

steps.what: Examine tags on the actual garment and read the written alteration marks or instructions
inputs: actual garment with attached alteration tags
outputs: tailor-read tag instructions and visible garment context

steps.what: Determine the alterations needed by interpreting the tags against the garment and flag unclear instructions
inputs: tailor-read tag instructions and visible garment context
actual garment construction and marked areas
outputs: tailor-understood alteration requirements or unresolved instruction

tasks.design: Keep direct tag examination and interpretation. A {OPS_SYSTEM} lookup or template would not remove handling and reading the short garment-specific instruction in this scenario; no additional record, report or send is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task requires reading the tag in its physical garment context rather than retrieving repeated reference data.
tasks.enabler_now: No justified software change is identified for this narrowly defined work.
tasks.still_hard: Handwritten marks and incomplete or ambiguous alterations need garment knowledge and clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret an instruction in relation to actual seams, fabric and fit without assuming an unclear mark is authoritative.

ambition.what: No additional service or authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0-0 because no system or access change is proposed

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: short physical alteration tags often need interpretation against the attached garment; automatic transcription alone does not perform that judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual stated tag examination and determining needed alterations. It includes neither performing the sewing nor an invented reporting baseline.
The tag writer supplies the actual attached instruction. The tailor physically reads it in s1 and interprets it in s2; no free structured tag data is assumed.

Before retaining zero, separately consider lookup, capture and send: this scenario needs no reference lookup or new persistent record and makes no transmission. If the workshop requires copying tags into an order record, that actual write must be added and native forms tested before declaring zero for the expanded task.
Native lookup and template configuration do not change the two stated steps here. No machine runtime or downstream sewing saving is claimed.
Shares are provisional scenario proportions, not measured baselines. All work is retained. Incremental upkeep is zero because nothing is introduced or reconfigured.
unknowns: Whether actual workshop practice requires a separate order update
Clarity and consistency of alteration tags
research_questions: Is there an actual repeated lookup or duplicate record write beyond reading the attached tag?
Would photographing the tag add capture effort without changing interpretation?

incremental.description: No new tool, rule or integration is introduced, so there is no ongoing upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both tag handling/reading and garment-context interpretation remain fully human; no actual record or lookup change has been identified in this task boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The tailor can spend less time finding references, repeating identifiers and calculating costs, while measurements, customer choices and garment judgement remain hands-on.
role.ambitious_version: Compare a feasible material or finish alternative with a transparent cost estimate while preserving the personal fitting conversation.
